bridge: Builds on M01 arithmetic and P02 tracing. Read the notation here before the formal lecture; no proof-writing experience is assumed.
teaching:
A proposition is a statement with a truth value. AND requires both statements to be true; OR requires at least one; NOT reverses a truth value. An implication P implies Q rules out the case where P is true and Q false. It does not assert that Q implies P. This distinction appears in access-control policies and proofs.

A set is a collection of distinct elements. A function maps each input in its domain to exactly one output in its codomain. A graph has vertices and edges; a directed edge records direction. A state machine adds states and transitions, allowing you to reason about every permitted next step rather than one observed execution.

A proof explains why a claim follows from assumptions. For an invariant, show it holds initially and that each permitted transition preserves it. Induction follows the same structure: establish a base case, assume a claim for an arbitrary step and prove the next. One successful test is evidence about one execution, while an invariant argument covers all executions allowed by the model.
example:
P Q | P AND Q | P implies Q
F F | F       | T
F T | F       | T
T F | F       | F
T T | T       | T

Door states: Locked, Unlocked
unlock: Locked -> Unlocked, requires valid_key
lock: Unlocked -> Locked
Invariant: unlock succeeds only if valid_key is true.
explanation: The implication is true when P is false because it forbids only a true premise with a false conclusion. For the door model, inspect every transition into Unlocked: the listed unlock transition requires a key. If a new emergency transition bypasses that guard, the proof must include it and the invariant may fail. A proof is only as complete as its model.
exercise: Build the truth table for NOT(P AND Q) and compare it with (NOT P) OR (NOT Q). Then add a maintenance transition to the door that requires admin=true. State a corrected authorisation invariant covering both routes.
solution: The two expressions match in all four rows: T,T,T,F for FF,FT,TF,TT. The revised condition is that unlock requires valid_key OR admin, with each transition enforcing its own guard.
challenge: An account starts balance=0. Deposit adds a nonnegative integer; withdraw subtracts an integer only when 0<=amount<=balance. Prove balance>=0 is invariant, then identify a guard removal that invalidates the proof.
challenge_solution: Base: zero is nonnegative. Deposit preserves it by adding a nonnegative value. Withdraw preserves it because amount<=balance. Removing that upper bound permits a negative balance. State integer/nonnegative assumptions explicitly rather than silently changing the model.
